anyOf.description: It finished its answer.
The provider cut the answer off at its output token limit.
The model refused.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

AnswerStop.description: Why the model stopped at its final answer.

ApprovalAsk.description:
A tool asks to use a capability its session's permission mode does not
grant on its own.

reason.description: Why the policy asks, in its words.

anyOf.description: One of Rho's own tools.

A tool a host or integration provides, such as an MCP server's: a
different trust boundary from Rho's own.
Rho itself, as when it builds a prompt.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

May a tool use a capability? Answer [`InputAnswer::AllowOnce`],
[`InputAnswer::AllowForSession`], or [`InputAnswer::Deny`].

May the session leave plan mode to carry out its plan? Answer
[`InputAnswer::ApprovePlan`] or [`InputAnswer::KeepPlanning`].

Questions for the user. Answer [`InputAnswer::Answers`],
[`InputAnswer::Decline`], or [`InputAnswer::Dismiss`].
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

Every subagent run of every session the daemon hosts:
`behavior.agent_concurrency` in the daemon's config.

Claude-cli subagent runs, nested under [`Self::AgentConcurrency`]:
`RHO_CLAUDE_AGENT_CONCURRENCY` in the daemon's environment.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

Budget.description:
A concurrency budget jobs wait on, named for the setting that sizes it.
Protocol minors may add budgets.

value.description: What an answer sends when it picks this choice.

ClientInfo.description: Who is connecting. Logged by the daemon; never used for authorization.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

ContentBlock.description: One piece of a user message.

Cursor.description: Where a client is in a session's stream; send it back to resume.

jobs.description:
Jobs with a turn in progress: [`crate::JobState::Running`] or
[`crate::JobState::WaitingForInput`].

socket.description: The socket the daemon listens on.

started_at.description: Unix time, in seconds, when the daemon started.

DefaultAnswer.description: The answer the agent suggests for a question.

values.description:
What the answer would send: the value of each choice it names, or
the agent's own text where it names none.

anyOf.description: Pre-select it.
Only focus or mark it, so the user still picks it.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

DefaultStyle.description: How a client offers a question's suggested answer.

anyOf.description: The client fell too far behind; reattach with its cursor.
The daemon is stopping.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

DetachReason.description: Why the daemon dropped an attachment.

capabilities.description:
Optional features this daemon supports. Protocol minors add names
here; protocol 1.0 defines none.

protocol.description: The protocol the daemon speaks. Its major equals the client's.

InputAnswer.description:
An answer to an input request. Each [`Ask`] lists the answers it takes;
any other is [`crate::ErrorCode::InvalidParams`].

oneOf.description: Approve this one use of the capability.
Approve this exact use for the rest of the session.
Refuse it; the tool learns `reason`, or that the user denied it.

Leave plan mode and carry out the plan in `mode`, one of the
request's `modes`.

Answers keyed by question id: the values of the chosen choices, or
the user's own text where a question allows it.
The user declined to answer the questions.
The user dismissed the questions without choosing.

InputRequest.description: One thing a turn waits on a person for.

timeout.description:
When the daemon answers the request itself, if it will; absent once
the request is held.

tool_call.description: The tool call that asks, when a tool call does.

InputRequestId.description:
Identifies one input request among its session's, for as long as the
daemon has the session loaded.

InputTimeout.description:
An answer the daemon gives an input request at a deadline, unless a
client answers the request or holds it first. Only a question whose
agent offered fallback answers, in a session whose user set
`[questionnaire] timeout_seconds`, has one (#1660).

deadline_ms.description: Unix time, in milliseconds, when the daemon answers.

reason.description: Why the agent offered that answer.

JobId.description: A job's id. Opaque to clients: send back the string the daemon gave.

anyOf.description: The turns of a session the daemon hosts; see [`super::SESSION_NEW`].

One subagent run, started by the session or workflow job that is its
[`JobSummary::parent`].

One drive of a workflow run, started by the session job that is its
[`JobSummary::parent`]; the run's agent nodes are its child
[`JobKind::Subagent`] jobs.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

JobKind.description: What a job runs. Protocol minors may add kinds.

anyOf.description: Created; no turn has started.

A subagent run waiting for capacity; [`JobSummary::queue`] says
where it stands.

The turn waits for an approval, a plan approval, or a question to be
answered with [`super::SESSION_ANSWER`]. Nothing is denied because no
client is attached; the wait ends with an answer, a cancel, or a
timeout the user configured ([`super::InputTimeout`]).
The turn failed; [`JobSummary::error`] says why.
The daemon stopped, or died, before the turn ended.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

JobState.description:
Where a job is. A session job's state is that of its current or last
turn; a subagent job's is that of its one run.
Protocol minors may add states.

created_at.description: Unix time, in seconds, when the job was created.

error.description: Why the job failed, when its state is [`JobState::Failed`].

parent.description: The job that started this one; `None` for a job a client started.

queue.description:
Where the job waits for capacity, when its state is
[`JobState::Queued`].

session.description:
The Rho session the job writes; `None` for a subagent run on another
runtime (Claude, Cursor, Antigravity), which keeps its own.

updated_at.description: Unix time, in seconds, of the job's last state change.

workflow_run.description: The workflow run a [`JobKind::Workflow`] job drives.

workspace.description: The workspace the job runs in.

Location.description: A file a tool call touches, and the line when one applies.

MessageId.description:
Identifies one message in a session's event stream: chunks with the
same id extend one message.

anyOf.description:
Run `program` with `args` in `cwd`. `shell_command` is the command
line, when the program is a shell running one.
Reach the network, at `url` when the tool names one.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

Operation.description: What a capability would let a tool do.

anyOf.description: Under the session's workspace.
Under a directory the user added to the session, `root`.
Anywhere: outside every root the session knows.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

PathScope.description: Where a path an operation names lies.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

PermissionMode.description: A session's permission mode, as `/permissions` names it.

PlanApprovalAsk.description: The session, in plan mode, asks to carry out its plan.

modes.description:
The permission modes the session may carry the plan out in; an
approval names one.

PlanEntry.description: One step of the agent's plan.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

ProtocolVersion.description:
A protocol version. Minors add optional fields, methods, and error codes;
majors may change anything.

Question.description: One question, with the choices it offers.

allow_other.description: Whether an answer may give its own text instead of a choice.

default.description: The answer the agent suggests, if any.

header.description: A short label for the question, such as a tab title.

id.description: Names the question in an answer's `answers`.

required.description: Whether an answer must answer this question.

selection.description: How many choices an answer may pick.

QuestionAsk.description: Questions the agent asks the user, answered together.

QueuePlace.description:
Where a queued job waits: the budget it waits on, that budget's limit,
and its place in the budget's queue.

limit.description: How many runs the budget lets run at once.

position.description: 1 for the job that starts when the next slot frees.

Replay.description:
What the events after a [`SessionAttachResponse`] start with.

Closed on purpose, unlike the event enums: a client cannot follow events
it does not know how to start from, so a new kind is a protocol major.

oneOf.description: The events after the client's cursor follow.

Discard what you have for this session, cursor included: its saved
transcript follows, then the turn in progress.

anyOf.description: A client answered it.
The turn no longer waits for it, as when the turn was cancelled.

Nobody answered or held it by its timeout's deadline, so the daemon
answered it with the timeout's answer.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

Resolution.description:
How an input request closed, as [`super::SessionEvent::InputResolved`]
tells every attached client.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

Selection.description: How many choices a question's answer may pick.

Seq.description:
Position in a stream: the number of live events sent before and
including this one, from 1. `Seq(0)` is not a position: a reset's
transcript events carry it (see [`super::SessionEventParams::seq`]), and
a cursor at 0 always resets.

answer.description: One of the answers the request's [`Ask`] lists.

SessionAnswerResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_ANSWER`]: the answer won, and the daemon handed it
to the turn. An answer that lost, to another client's or to the turn
withdrawing the request, is [`crate::ErrorCode::InputNotOpen`]. A turn
that stops waiting at the same moment, because it was cancelled or the
tool that asked gave up, ignores an answer that won.

after.description:
The last event this client has, to resume after it. Absent, from
another stream, or older than the daemon keeps: [`Replay::Reset`].

SessionAttachResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_ATTACH`]. The session's events then arrive as
[`SESSION_EVENT`] notifications, never before this response. Attaching
again on the same connection replaces the earlier attachment.

inputs.description:
The input requests open when the attachment began, oldest first:
what a client may answer even when the replay no longer holds the
events that opened them (#1660). The replay may repeat some; an
input request's id names it.

state.description: The session's job state when the attachment began.

stream.description: The stream the events belong to; a cursor names it to resume.

SessionCancelResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_CANCEL`]: the turn in progress, if any, has been
asked to stop. The turn saves what it did and ends
[`crate::JobState::Cancelled`], or [`crate::JobState::Interrupted`] when
the daemon is stopping. A cancel that arrives before a prompted turn
begins still cancels it, and that prompt answers
[`crate::ErrorCode::TurnCancelled`].

SessionDetachResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_DETACH`]: no events of the session follow. Detaching
a session this connection has not attached also succeeds.

SessionDetachedParams.description:
Params of the [`SESSION_DETACHED`] notification. No events of the
session follow; attach again, with the client's cursor, to resume.

anyOf.description:
The session's job changed state: a turn started (`running`), waits
for input, or ended. An ended turn's [`Self::TurnEnded`] comes first.
A user message, whole.
More of the agent's reply.
More of the agent's reasoning.
Opens or updates a tool call; absent fields are unchanged.
The agent's plan, replacing any earlier one.
How full the model's context is.

A titled card the session shows outside the conversation, such as a
background result.
Something to tell the user that is not part of the conversation.

The turn waits for a person to answer `request` with
[`super::SESSION_ANSWER`] (#1660).

Input request `id` closed: a client answered it, the turn withdrew
it, or it timed out. Clients that show it stop.
The turn ended, and how (#1669).

Input request `id`'s timeout stopped: a client held it with
[`super::SESSION_HOLD`], so it waits for an answer.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

SessionEvent.description: One thing that happened in a session.

seq.description:
Rises by one per live event. A reset's transcript events carry 0,
except the last, which carries the seq the turn in progress began
after. So the highest seq a client has seen since its attach
response, once above 0, is always a cursor it can resume from: one
that detaches partway through a transcript resets again.

SessionHoldResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_HOLD`]: the request no longer times out, and every
attached client saw [`super::SessionEvent::InputHeld`]. Holding a
request that has no timeout, or one already held, changes nothing. A
request that closed is [`crate::ErrorCode::InputNotOpen`].

SessionId.description:
A session's id, the one `rho sessions` and `/resume` show. Opaque to
clients: send back the string the daemon gave.

cwd.description:
The session's workspace, an absolute path to an existing directory.
The daemon reads config and agents for it as `rho` started there
would.

SessionNewResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_NEW`]: the session is loaded and its job is
[`crate::JobState::Idle`]. `rho sessions` lists the session once its
first prompt is saved; [`super::JOB_LIST`] shows its job.

text.description: The user message, sent to the model as written.

SessionPromptResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_PROMPT`]: the prompt is saved and its turn is
running. The turn runs on in the daemon; [`super::JOB_LIST`] reports how
it ends.

A turn that ends before its prompt is saved answers with an error
instead: [`crate::ErrorCode::TurnFailed`] with the reason,
[`crate::ErrorCode::TurnCancelled`] when a cancel stopped it, or
[`crate::ErrorCode::DaemonStopping`] when the daemon stopped it.

text.description: Input for the running turn's next model request.

SessionSteerResponse.description:
Result of [`SESSION_STEER`]: the input is queued for the running turn,
which applies it at its next model request. A turn that ends first drops
it.

StopResponse.description:
Result of [`DAEMON_STOP`]: the daemon has begun shutting down. It finishes
in-flight responses, closes connections, interrupts running turns, and
exits.

StreamId.description:
One loaded session's event stream. A new daemon, or a reload, starts
a new stream.

ToolCallId.description:
Identifies one tool call; every [`ToolCallUpdate`] with the same id
updates that call.

ToolCallUpdate.description:
Opens a tool call, or updates the one with the same `id`. Absent fields
are unchanged.

content.description: Replaces the call's content when present.

raw_input.description: The tool's input, as the model wrote it.

anyOf.description: A file change; `old_text` is absent for a new file.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

ToolContent.description: One piece of what a tool call shows.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

ToolKind.description: What a tool does, so a client can pick an icon or a layout.

anyOf.description: Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

message.description:
What went wrong, for a person. An authentication failure names only
the provider and auth and how to log in, never the provider's own
text, which may echo credentials.

anyOf.description: The provider rejected the credentials, or there were none.
The provider failed the request.
A tool's host failed, not just one tool call.

The session's config cannot run, such as a model the provider does
not offer.
Anything else.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

TurnErrorKind.description: What kind of failure ended a turn.

anyOf.description:
The model gave its final answer. `text` is the answer whole, as the
turn saved it, which a client that missed chunks or saw a provider
retry restart a reply can show instead of what it gathered.

The turn used its model-step limit before the model answered; `text`
is the reply text of its last step, possibly empty.
A client cancelled it.
The daemon stopped, or died, before it ended.
It failed.
Any other value: one a later protocol minor adds.

VersionFix.description: Which side of an incompatible pair has to change.

oneOf.description:
The running daemon is older than the client. Stopping it lets the next
connection start the daemon from the newer installed binary.
The client is older than the daemon. Update the client.

VersionMismatch.description:
An incompatible handshake. The daemon sends this as the `data` of a
[`crate::ErrorCode::VersionMismatch`] error; its `Display` is the
actionable message for users.
